The TokenBucketLimiter class is a rate limiter that allows short bursts but caps the sustained number of calls per second. It uses a token bucket algorithm to manage the rate of requests. The class has two private properties: `available` and `lastRefill`, which represent the number of tokens available and the last time the tokens were refilled, respectively. The constructor initializes these properties based on the capacity and refill rate. The `tryAcquire` method attempts to acquire a token by refilling the bucket and checking if there are any tokens available. If there are, it decrements the available tokens and returns true; otherwise, it returns false. The `refill` method updates the available tokens based on the elapsed time since the last refill.

Yes, when a call to an upstream service fails temporarily, it is retried. This is handled by the `retryWithBackoff` function in `retry-policy.ts`. The price at the bottom of the basket is calculated by summing up the total price of each line item in the cart. Each line item's price is calculated by multiplying the unit price in cents by the quantity of that item. This sum is then returned as the total price of the basket.

User passwords are stored safely by hashing them using a salt. The `hashPassword` function in `src/auth/password-hasher.ts` generates a random salt and combines it with the plain password to create a hash. The hash is then stored in the database. The `verifyPassword` function uses the same salt to verify a login attempt by comparing the stored hash with the hash of the provided plain password. This ensures that even if the database is compromised, the passwords cannot be easily read.

To check a login attempt against the stored password without leaking timing information, we use the `verifyPassword` function from `src/auth/password-hasher.ts`. This function compares a plain text password with a stored hash in constant time. It splits the stored hash into a salt and an expected hash, then derives the actual hash from the plain text password using the same salt. It compares the actual hash with the expected hash, ensuring that the comparison is done in constant time regardless of the length of the hashes.

A thrown error ends up as an API response through the `toHttpResponse` function in `src/errors/error-handler.ts`. This function checks the type of the error and returns a `HttpErrorResponse` object with appropriate status and body. If the error is an instance of `ValidationError`, it returns a response with the error's status code and a body containing the error message and field. If the error is an instance of `AppError`, it returns a response with the error's status code and a body containing only the error message. If the error is neither, it returns a generic 500 status code with a message indicating an unexpected error.
